brief: Monday GS TMT spec-sales note, mostly a news roundup with limited argued causal chains rather than one thesis. US equities closed a three-day losing streak Friday as oil eased on hopes of renewed US-Iran talks. The 30-year Treasury yield rose to 5.53%, its highest since 2004, as hawkish Fed commentary and strong flash PMIs pushed yields to post-2007 highs before Friday's relief on Iran de-escalation reports. Market breadth has narrowed to its lowest since the Dot-Com Bubble even though AI strength keeps the headline S&P 500 resilient: the median stock trades 16% below its 52-week high. Oracle's CDS hit a record high and its 2056 bond yield crossed 8% as credit markets question who funds the next $1tn of data-center spend, widening spreads across AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, META and NVDA. Meta's Muse app topped app-store charts with 900k+ downloads in six days, driving an 11% Monday rally and reviving momentum trades. This week's focus names are Micron (GIR sees upside to consensus) and Accenture (bookings softened, guidance narrowed). Extensive semis, fintech and telecom M&A news is reported without a house view attached.
